title: Multiple regions, delayed replicas and scaling reads

videos.script: A standby next to the primary survives the loss of a server. Losing a whole region needs a copy far away, and far away cannot be synchronous. {{far}} You build a standby fed by a standby, so one copy of the log crosses the distance. {{cascade}} You run a report on a standby, and watch it cancelled to let replication go on. Then you turn on feedback, and the primary keeps a thousand dead rows for it instead. {{reads}} Last, a replica two minutes behind on purpose. A delete runs on the primary, and you copy the fifty lost orders back out of the replica before it applies the delete itself. {{delay}}
